hook.text: BP rebranded as 'Beyond Petroleum' in 2000 while spending 96% of its budget on fossil fuels.

buildup.text: Greenwashing uses environmental language to sell the appearance of sustainability without the substance.

discovery.text: BP also invented the 'personal carbon footprint' to shift climate blame from corporations to individual consumers.

twist.text: In 2010, the Deepwater Horizon spill killed 11 workers and spewed 210 million gallons of oil.

climax.text: Greenwashing shows that propaganda backfires when reality contradicts the message spectacularly.

punchline.text: Beyond Petroleum, then the worst oil spill in history. Copy can't hide reality.

quiz.question: What concept did BP invent to shift climate blame to consumers?

details.summary: Greenwashing is the practice of making misleading environmental claims to appear more sustainable than you are. Companies use vague terms like 'eco-friendly' and 'natural,' green-tinted packaging, and cherry-picked data to exploit growing environmental concerns without making real changes.
details.whyItMatters: As climate awareness grows, greenwashing proliferates. Learning to spot it empowers consumers to reward genuinely sustainable companies and punish those hiding behind propaganda.
takeaways: Vague claims like 'eco-friendly' and 'natural' are common greenwashing signals
Green packaging and nature imagery create false environmental associations
Third-party certifications are more reliable than self-reported claims

faq.question: What are the most common greenwashing tactics?
faq.answer: Vague language ('eco-friendly,' 'all-natural'), irrelevant claims (CFC-free when CFCs are already banned), hidden trade-offs (one green feature masking major environmental harm), and misleading imagery (green colors and nature photos on polluting products).

faq.question: How can I identify greenwashing?
faq.answer: Look for specific, verifiable claims rather than vague language. Check for third-party certifications like B Corp or Fair Trade. Research the company's overall environmental record, not just the claim on one product. If it sounds too good and too easy, it probably is.
